newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH shares fall on DFS profit worries.
newsitem.headline: LVMH shares fall on DFS profit worries.

text.p: Shares of French luxury goods group LVMH slid five percent on Friday on what financial analysts said were investor worries about profits at newly acquired U.S. duty free chain giant DFS.
The company's shares finished 70 francs lower at 1,333, despite a statement by LVMH that its 1996 provisional net attributable operating profit would be up six percent from 1995.

"The impact on the 1996 results from DFS on the proforma accounts of LVMH should be strongly positive at the net operating level -- before exceptional items and goodwill -- and very slightly dilutive on the net result," LVMH said in the statement.

LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton had warned previously that its $2.6 billion acquisition of 61.25 percent of DFS last year would weigh on earnings per share for 1997 but said it was targeting higher sales and profits before the impact of the acquisition.
A spokeswoman declined to comment on market talk that DFS could see profits down 15 percent in 1996 and that if the Japanese yen weakened further, DFS profits could fall a further 20 percent in 1997.

"Even if the LVMH statement is trying to smooth the news from DHS, they are not denying it," one Paris analyst said. "The deal looks strategically good but not so good in its short-term and mid-term impact on the bottom line.

The acquisition of San Francisco-based DFS reinforces LVMH's presence around the lucrative Pacific Rim and extends its control over the sale of its luxury products, ranging from Moet & Chandon champagnes to Christian Dior perfumes and Louis Vuitton designer luggage.
LVMH added in the statement that talks with Robert Miller, a minority holder of Duty Free Shoppers (DFS), could end soon and on terms close to LVMH's original acquisition of DFS stock.

"The LVMH group moreover (expects) the negotiations with Mr Robert Miller for the acquisition of his holding in DFS could be concluded soon on conditions close to those for the purchases already made," it said.
Meanwhile, Standard & Poor's reaffirmed its A-1+ on LVMH's French commercial paper programme.
"The rating affirmation reflects the improvement of LVMH's competitive positions in the luxury goods business, despite a much weaker financial flexibility," it said in a statement.
